Using the focus-directrix property, for \(B=(t^2,2t)\) on \(y^2=4x\),

\[
BF=\text{distance from }B\text{ to directrix }x=-1=t^2+1.
\]

Let \(M=(-1,2t)\) be the foot of \(B\) on the directrix. Then

\[
AB+BF=AB+BM \ge AM \ge \text{distance from }A(5,4)\text{ to }x=-1=6.
\]

Equality occurs when \(2t=4\), so \(t=2\), giving \(B=(4,4)\). Thus the perimeter is minimized at \(B=(4,4)\).

Now with \(A(5,4)\), \(B(4,4)\), and \(F(1,0)\), the area is

\[
\frac12 \cdot AB \cdot \text{height}
=\frac12 \cdot 1 \cdot 4=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
